# Collective reservation and compilation protocol, version 3.0.0

Implement a persistent, offline controller for recurring nonuniform allgather jobs.
The provided collective pipeline, topology and XML modules form a working legacy
codebase. Extend or replace its internals to meet this contract. Its equal-shard,
floating-point throughput interface is not the service specified here. No legacy
function, source-file layout, optimization method or particular output ordering is
mandatory. All requirements below apply to the collected service.

## Execution and artifact

Submit `/workspace/submission/`, an ordinary directory containing `main.py` and any
ordinary supporting files/directories: at most 256 entries and 1 MiB of file bytes.
Harmless extra files are allowed within these budgets. Symlinks, hard-linked files,
devices, sockets and FIFOs are rejected. Only this directory is collected.
The runner invokes `python3 -I -B /workspace/submission/main.py` once per trace.
Explicitly add the script directory to `sys.path` for local imports under `-I`.
Python 3.11.14 and its standard library are available. The fixed, read-only wheel
`/workspace/vendor/networkx-3.4.2-py3-none-any.whl` is available in every worker;
add this path to `sys.path` to use NetworkX 3.4.2. No optional backend or package
installation is required. The wheel's BSD license and the legacy Apache license
are included. There is no GPU, network, subprocess, or external service requirement.

One UTF-8 JSON value arrives on each input line. Emit exactly one UTF-8 JSON object
and newline per line, in order, before accepting EOF. Retain state between lines
and flush replies; emit no other stdout. Final input newline is optional. JSON
whitespace and CRLF are allowed. Blank lines, BOM, duplicate object keys, nonfinite
numbers, invalid UTF-8, unrecognized fields/operations and wrong types are invalid.
All integer fields require JSON integers: booleans, decimals and exponent forms do
not qualify. Invalid commands return exactly `{"status":"invalid"}` and have no
effect. Malformed input never terminates the service or resets its state.
A trace has at most 256 lines, each at most 131072 bytes including its newline,
and at most TWO distinct `id` values among schema-valid `prepare` commands, including
stale attempts and retries. These are input-domain guarantees. Other malformed
commands may occur. A successful `load` occurs at most once; repeat loads are tested.

The budget per trace is 60 seconds wall and CPU time, 1 GiB address space, one
process and one thread; fork/clone and network operations are blocked. Do not launch subprocesses.
The local worker has one effective CPU selected from the assigned two-core pool;
the agent/build environment is assigned two cores. Exec may replace a process,
but cannot create an additional process or reset a trace.
The effective soft/hard FD ceiling is 64, INCLUDING inherited streams 0, 1 and 2:
when those are the only open descriptors, 61 additional descriptor slots remain.
Stdout is bounded by 64 MiB and stderr by 256 KiB per trace. The only writable
scratch directory is `/workspace/tmp`; use at most 64 MiB, 1024 entries, and 16 MiB
per file. No files persist between traces. Avoid pycache writes (`-B` is supplied).
The budget accommodates two large compilation proposals plus controller traffic
in a CPU-only reservation service; it is not a measured collective execution time.

`public_check.py` checks only the supplied tiny format/metadata fixture. It never
runs a submission, computes admission, audits schedules or simulates the controller.
Its success alone says nothing about full service correctness. For a local sanity
run: `python3 -I -B submission/main.py < examples/requests.jsonl > /workspace/tmp/answers.jsonl`,
then `python3 -I -B public_check.py examples/requests.jsonl /workspace/tmp/answers.jsonl`.
The public workspace and candidate artifact contain no private tests or reference.

## Common schema and graph

Objects have exactly the fields specified below. Lists may be empty unless a
minimum is given. `ID` and `owner` strings match `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,32}` using ASCII.
A tick, capacity, rate or chunk amount is an integer in [0,10^12]. Period is an
integer in [1,10^6]; expected `rev` is in [0,10^12]. Node references in operation
schemas are integers in [0,47], link references in [0,127]. A schema-valid reference
outside the loaded graph produces `REFERENCE` where specified, not `invalid`.

A `window` is `[s,e]` with 0<=s<e<=10^12, representing [s,e). An `envelope` is a
list of at most 128 distinct `[link_id,rate]` pairs, each rate in [1,10^12]; omitted
links have rate zero. An envelope reserves this rate in EACH direction, independently.

`{"op":"load","n":N,"links":[[u,v,capacity],...],"bookings":[BOOKING,...]}`
initializes the service. 2<=N<=48, vertices are 0..N-1, and there are 0..128 links.
Link endpoints must be distinct loaded vertices; unordered endpoint pairs must be
unique. Link ID is its position in this list, and endpoint order fixes direction
0 as u->v, direction 1 as v->u. Capacity is the per-direction base rate, including
zero. Opposite directions have separate equal budgets; they do not share one budget.
`BOOKING` has exactly `id,owner,window,envelope`. There are at most 128 bookings,
with distinct IDs and at most 2048 envelope entries in total. Booking references
must exist. Every initial booking is committed, and at every tick and link the
sum of active booking rates must not exceed base capacity. Violating these structural load relations is `invalid`; overbooking is checked
only when initializing the first load. A later structurally valid load returns
ALREADY_LOADED without evaluating its booking overlaps. No connectivity, positive-capacity or feasible-job assumption
is made about the graph. Structural load checks are schema validity; first-load overlap failure also returns invalid.

`{"op":"about"}` returns exactly
`{"status":"ok","protocol":"forest-controller/3"}` without changing anything.
Initially the service is unloaded, with revision 0 and time 0. A valid first load
returns `{"status":"ok","rev":0,"now":0}`. A schema-valid later load returns
`{"status":"error","code":"ALREADY_LOADED","rev":R}`. Schema validation still
comes first. Well-formed operations other than about/load before initialization
return `{"status":"error","code":"NOT_LOADED","rev":0}`.

## State, errors and capacity

After initialization write R for current revision and T for current time. A live
lease is an unexpired committed booking, including a booking which starts later.
At tick t, it consumes its full envelope iff s<=t<e. Preparations consume no rate.
Let used(l,t) be the sum of rates on link l of those active live leases.
An offered envelope b for [s,e) fits iff used(l,t)+b(l)<=capacity(l) for every
link and every t in [s,e). The endpoints and all arithmetic are exact integers.

A successful advance, edit, first commit, or cancel increments R by one, including
a successful no-op advance/edit. Other operations, blocked edits, all errors,
invalid commands and all replays leave revision and resource state unchanged.
No operation changes graph endpoints or link IDs after load. A base-capacity edit
applies uniformly to now and all future ticks. Time never advances implicitly.
Expired/cancelled/force-revoked IDs retain history and cannot become live again.

Unless stated otherwise a state error has exactly `status:"error",code:CODE,rev:R`;
a revision failure has exactly `status:"stale",rev:R`. Schema/JSON validity precedes
all state conditions. The priorities within each operation are specified below;
these priorities resolve commands with multiple faults, rather than selecting an
optimization procedure. All replies have exactly their stated fields. Object-key
order is immaterial. Sorted ID arrays use ASCII lexicographic order.

## Controller operations

`{"op":"audit","at":[t,...]}` accepts at most eight ticks, including duplicates.
A tick below T gives `TIME`. Otherwise reply
`{"status":"ok","rev":R,"now":T,"leases":[sorted live IDs],"samples":[[t,[a0,...,aM-1]],...]}`.
Samples preserve requested order and duplicates; a_l=capacity(l)-used(l,t).
Audit does not expose preparations or historical dead IDs and does not advance time.

`{"op":"advance","time":t}` gives `TIME` when t<T. Otherwise time becomes t,
leases with end<=t expire, R increments, and reply is
`{"status":"ok","rev":newR,"now":t,"expired":[sorted expired IDs]}`.
A lease starting exactly at t is active; a lease ending exactly at t is expired.

`{"op":"edit","rev":r,"changes":[[link_id,new_capacity],...],"force":BOOL}`
contains at most 128 distinct link IDs. Its state priorities are expected revision
r=R, then all referenced links existing. A mismatch gives stale or REFERENCE.
Apply the listed changes as one proposed vector. With force=false, if this would
overbook any live lease at any integer t>=T, return
`{"status":"blocked","rev":R,"link":l,"time":t,"used":u,"capacity":c}`,
where u=used(l,t)>c=the proposed capacity of l. Any such witness is valid.
The entire edit has no effect when blocked. Otherwise apply it and increment R.
With force=true, first revoke ALL live leases with positive rate on ANY link whose
capacity actually decreases, even if the decrease would have been safe. Apply all
changes atomically and increment R. Equal-capacity writes and increases do not
revoke leases. Both successful forms return
`{"status":"ok","rev":newR,"cancelled":[sorted revoked IDs]}`.
Safe nonforced edits return an empty cancelled array.

`{"op":"prepare","id":ID,"owner":OWNER,"window":[s,e],"period":p,"participants":[[v,r_v],...],"envelope":[[l,b_l],...],"rev":r}`
requests compilation of a recurring allgather proposal. Participants are 2..32
unique vertices, each chunk demand in [0,10^12], with positive total demand D.
A zero-demand participant is still a receiver and may forward as a compute vertex.
Other graph vertices are ordinary unicast forwarders. Each period p the job
collects every source's r_v chunks at every participant, using only its offered
envelope. Duration must be a positive multiple of p, and s>=T.

A prepare's identity binds its entire payload including owner, window, period,
expected revision, participants and envelope. Ordering participants/envelope pairs
is ignored for identity; other values must match exactly. For an already recorded
ID with the same prepare payload, return
`{"status":"replay","id":ID,"rev":R,"base_rev":originalR,"outcome":"prepared" or "denied"}`.
This is historical metadata: no certificate is repeated, no lease is installed,
and dead IDs remain dead. An existing ID with a different prepare payload, or any
ID originating in load, gives CONFLICT. These cache checks precede revision checks.
For a new ID, the priorities are: expected revision r=R, all references existing,
s>=T, and duration divisible by p. Failures give stale, REFERENCE, TIME or WINDOW.
Such failures are not recorded and the ID can be retried. Successfully prepared or
denied proposals are recorded forever within the trace; neither changes R.

If the offered envelope fits the current lease book AND the network certificate
below exists, reply `{"status":"prepared","id":ID,"rev":R,"plan":PLAN}` and
remember base revision R. It is mandatory to prepare whenever both conditions hold.
If either condition fails, reply with one of these valid negative certificates:
`{"status":"denied","id":ID,"rev":R,"kind":"capacity","link":l,"time":t,"used":u,"capacity":c}`,
where s<=t<e, u=used(l,t)+b_l>c=current base capacity; OR
`{"status":"denied","id":ID,"rev":R,"kind":"cut","cut":[vertices...]}`
with the strict deficient-cut condition below. Either valid denial is accepted when
both obstructions exist. No preferred cut, link, tick or schedule is required.

`{"op":"commit","id":ID,"owner":OWNER,"rev":r}` has these state priorities:
unknown ID gives MISSING; wrong owner gives OWNER; an already live committed ID
returns `{"status":"ok","id":ID,"rev":R,"replay":true}` even if r is old;
a recorded dead ID gives GONE; a denied ID gives DENIED. For a prepared ID, both
r and its base revision must equal R, otherwise stale. A fresh successful commit
installs the ENTIRE offered envelope and window, increments R, and returns
`{"status":"ok","id":ID,"rev":newR,"replay":false}`. It never reserves merely
the physical loads of one returned plan. This makes state independent of valid
certificate choices. Stale preparations remain historical and cannot be rebased;
use the other permitted proposal ID for a new payload. A committed retry cannot
resurrect an expired, cancelled or force-revoked lease.

`{"op":"cancel","id":ID,"owner":OWNER,"rev":r}` has priorities r=R, ID being
a live committed lease, then matching owner; failures are stale, MISSING, OWNER.
Success releases the entire envelope, marks the ID dead, increments R and returns
`{"status":"ok","rev":newR,"released":ID}`. Repeated cancellation gives MISSING.
Prepared and denied IDs cannot be cancelled; they are not live leases.

## Network objective and certificates

The objective is exact admission and a realizable aggregate-throughput schedule,
not minimum finite-message latency or a particular tree/hop count. Switches cannot
multicast or aggregate. Every logical send has separate charged unicast traffic.
A compute receiver may replicate the chunks it receives along its logical tree.
A period provides integer physical chunk capacity c_l=p*b_l in EACH direction;
lease duration does not multiply this per-period budget. No rounding or epsilon
is permitted; quantities can exceed machine-word sizes in intermediate arithmetic.

A PLAN has exactly `trees,routes,recipes`. `trees` has at most 8192 records
`[root,count,[[u,v],...]]`. Each count is a positive integer <=D. Each record is a
logical directed out-tree on ALL participants: exactly |C|-1 distinct directed
edges, root indegree zero, every other participant indegree one, and every
participant reachable from root. Edges join distinct participants. For each root v,
the sum of its record counts is EXACTLY r_v (so zero-demand roots have no record).
Duplicated whole tree records are allowed; their weights add. Their order is free.
Let L(u,v) be the sum of counts of tree records containing logical edge u->v.

`recipes` is an acyclic serial-route circuit with at most 65536 nodes, indexed by
array position. A node is `[0,link_id,direction]`, denoting that single directed
physical link, or `[1,left_id,right_id]`, denoting the left walk followed by the
right walk. References may point earlier OR later. The two walks must have matching
end/start vertex w, and w MUST NOT be a participant. The concatenation retains the
first start and last end. All referenced IDs/links must exist, and the entire
circuit, including unused nodes, must be acyclic and well-typed. Sharing and unused
nodes are allowed. A finite expanded walk may revisit forwarding vertices or links;
no simplicity or maximum expanded length is imposed. Its every traversal is charged.

`routes` has at most 32768 records `[u,v,count,recipe_id]`, with distinct participant
endpoints u,v, integer count in [1,D], and a recipe denoting a walk exactly from u
to v. For EACH ordered participant pair the route counts sum EXACTLY to L(u,v).
Multiple routing entries and shared recipe roots are allowed. These integer route
pools may be assigned independently to occurrences of that logical edge in the
weighted tree copies. No per-chunk expansion or correlated route choice is required.

Every route record contributes its count copies of its expanded serial walk.
Each leaf occurrence contributes that multiplicity to its physical link/direction.
In a concatenation BOTH children carry the full multiplicity; sharing a recipe or
referencing one child twice does not grant a multicast discount. The aggregate
load on each physical link/direction must be <=p*b_l. There are no other capacity
pools or compute limits. Any PLAN satisfying these equalities and inequalities is
accepted. There is no canonical tie-break on tree, route or circuit representation.

A cut denial lists distinct vertices S within the loaded graph, in any order,
containing at least one but not all participants. It must satisfy the STRICT
integer inequality

    sum(p*b_l for physical links with exactly one endpoint in S)
      < sum(r_v for participants v in S).

Each crossing undirected link contributes once, because this is capacity in the
outgoing direction of the cut. Nonparticipants may belong to either side. This
certificate and PLAN feasibility are exact alternatives for the symmetric model.
All zero-demand participants still count when deciding whether S separates C.
All certificate bounds above apply to representation size, not hidden tie-breaks.

def a100_topology(nnode: int):
    G = nx.DiGraph()

            G.add_edge((a, "GPU", b), (a, "NVSwitch", 0), capacity=NVLINK_BW)

class SymmtricBranchingGenerator:
    SOURCE = "SOURCE"

    def __init__(self, topo: nx.DiGraph, k: int, syms: list[dict]):
        for a, b in topo.edges():
            assert 'capacity' in topo[a][b]
        self.N = topo.number_of_nodes()
        self.k = k
        self.compute_nodes = list(topo.nodes())

        assert OptimalBranchingsAlgo(topo, capacitated=True).test(1, k, False)

        self.flow_graph = nx.DiGraph(topo)
        self.s_nodes = {(u, 0): ('SOURCE', u, 0) for u in topo.nodes()}
        self.flow_graph.add_nodes_from(self.s_nodes.values())
        for (u, _), s in self.s_nodes.items():
            self.flow_graph.add_edge(SymmtricBranchingGenerator.SOURCE, s, capacity=k)
            self.flow_graph.add_edge(s, u)
        self.num_of_trees = len(self.s_nodes) * k

        self.syms = syms
        remain_nodes = set(topo.nodes())
        self.bases = set()
        for a in sorted(topo.nodes()):
            if a not in remain_nodes:
                continue
            self.bases.add(a)
            for sym in syms:
                b = sym[a]
                assert b in remain_nodes
                remain_nodes.remove(b)
        assert len(remain_nodes) == 0, "Check if identity is included in syms"
        self.bases = list(sorted(self.bases))
        assert topo.number_of_nodes() % len(self.bases) == 0

        self.Tcount = {u: 1 for u in self.bases}
        self.Ts = {(u, 0): [] for u in self.bases}
        self.Vs = {(u, 0): {u} for u in self.bases}
        self.Cs = {(u, 0): k for u in self.bases}

    def new_tree(self, root, edges, nodes, num) -> tuple:
        assert root in self.bases
        index = self.Tcount[root]
        self.Tcount[root] += 1
        self.Ts[root, index] = list(edges)
        self.Vs[root, index] = set(nodes)
        self.Cs[root, index] = num

        for sym in self.syms:
            s_node = ('SOURCE', sym[root], index)
            self.s_nodes[sym[root], index] = s_node
            self.flow_graph.add_node(s_node)
            self.flow_graph.add_edge(SymmtricBranchingGenerator.SOURCE, s_node, capacity=num)
            for v in nodes:
                self.flow_graph.add_edge(s_node, sym[v])

        return root, index

    def test_edge(self, w, j, x, y, nodes):
        for sym in self.syms:
            tmp_s_node = ('temp', self.s_nodes[sym[w], j])
            self.flow_graph.add_node(tmp_s_node)
            self.flow_graph.add_edge(SymmtricBranchingGenerator.SOURCE, tmp_s_node, capacity=0)
            for v in nodes:
                assert sym[v] != sym[y]
                self.flow_graph.add_edge(tmp_s_node, sym[v])
            self.flow_graph.add_edge(tmp_s_node, sym[y])

        chunks = 0
        momentum = 1
        while True:
            chunks += momentum
            if chunks > self.Cs[w, j] or chunks > self.flow_graph[x][y]['capacity']:
                chunks -= momentum
                if momentum == 1:
                    break
                else:
                    momentum = 1
                    continue
            for sym in self.syms:
                s_node = self.s_nodes[sym[w], j]
                assert chunks <= self.flow_graph[sym[x]][sym[y]]['capacity']
                self.flow_graph[sym[x]][sym[y]]['capacity'] -= chunks
                self.flow_graph[SymmtricBranchingGenerator.SOURCE][s_node]['capacity'] -= chunks
                self.flow_graph[SymmtricBranchingGenerator.SOURCE]['temp', s_node]['capacity'] += chunks
            res = True
            for v in self.compute_nodes:
                fval = nx.maximum_flow_value(self.flow_graph, SymmtricBranchingGenerator.SOURCE, v)
                if fval < self.num_of_trees - epsilon:
                    res = False
                    break
            for sym in self.syms:
                s_node = self.s_nodes[sym[w], j]
                self.flow_graph[sym[x]][sym[y]]['capacity'] += chunks
                self.flow_graph[SymmtricBranchingGenerator.SOURCE][s_node]['capacity'] += chunks
                self.flow_graph[SymmtricBranchingGenerator.SOURCE]['temp', s_node]['capacity'] -= chunks
            if res:
                momentum *= 2
            else:
                chunks -= momentum
                if momentum == 1:
                    break
                else:
                    momentum = 1

        for sym in self.syms:
            tmp_s_node = ('temp', self.s_nodes[sym[w], j])
            assert self.flow_graph[SymmtricBranchingGenerator.SOURCE][tmp_s_node]['capacity'] == 0
            self.flow_graph.remove_node(tmp_s_node)
        return chunks

    def generate(self) -> tuple[dict[tuple, list], dict[tuple, int]]:
        trees = sorted(self.Ts.keys())
        while len(trees) > 0:
            w, j = trees.pop(0)
            bfs_queue = list(self.Vs[w, j])
            while len(bfs_queue) > 0:
                x = bfs_queue.pop(0)
                assert x in self.Vs[w, j]
                for y in sorted(self.flow_graph.successors(x)):

def make_instance(rng):
    n = rng.randint(2, 8)

    for _ in range(m):

        key = (min(u,v), max(u,v))

    nlinks = len(links)
    period = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 5])

    crossing = sum(period*env.get(i,0) for i,(u,v,c) in enumerate(links) if (u in S) != (v in S))
    demand = sum(parts[v] for v in S if v in C)

import sys, random, json
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/submission')
import compiler

def tight_cuts(links, env, period, parts):
    """Count valid cuts where crossing == demand (either side)."""
    n = 0
    for (u,v,c) in links: n = max(n, u+1, v+1)
    for v in parts: n = max(n, v+1)
    C = set(parts)
    cnt = 0
    for mask in range(1, (1<<n) - 1):
        S = set(v for v in range(n) if mask >> v & 1)
        if not (S & C) or not (C - S):
            continue
        crossing = sum(period*env.get(i,0) for i,(u,v,c) in enumerate(links) if (u in S) != (v in S))
        d1 = sum(parts[v] for v in S if v in C)
        d2 = sum(parts[v] for v in C - S)
        if crossing == d1 or crossing == d2:
            cnt += 1
    return cnt

def make_instance(rng):
    n = rng.randint(3, 7)
    m = rng.randint(n, 12)
    links = []; seen = set()
    for _ in range(m):
        u = rng.randrange(n); v = rng.randrange(n)
        if u == v: continue
        key = (min(u,v), max(u,v))
        if key in seen: continue
        seen.add(key)
        links.append((u, v, 0))
    n = max([max(u,v) for (u,v,c) in links] + [1]) + 1
    period = rng.choice([1, 2, 3])
    env = {i: rng.randint(1, 3) for i in range(len(links)) if rng.random() < 0.9}
    npart = rng.randint(2, min(5, n))
    verts = rng.sample(range(n), npart)
    parts = {v: rng.randint(0, 3) for v in verts}
    if sum(parts.values()) == 0:
        parts[verts[0]] = 1
    return links, env, period, parts

rng = random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]))
N = int(sys.argv[2])
fails = 0; tightfeas = 0; feas = 0
for it in range(N):
    links, env, period, parts = make_instance(rng)
    if compiler.cut_witness(links, env, period, parts) is not None:
        continue
    feas += 1
    t = tight_cuts(links, env, period, parts)
    if t == 0:
        continue
    tightfeas += 1
    plan = compiler.compile_plan(links, env, period, parts)
    ok = compiler.verify_plan(links, env, period, parts, plan)
    if not ok:

    return compiler.cut_witness(links, env, period, parts) is None

def tighten(links, env, period, parts, rng):
    env = dict(env)
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        keys = list(env.keys())
        rng.shuffle(keys)
        for k in keys:

src = open('compiler.py').read()

# ---- add cut analysis helper after cut_witness ----
anchor = "# ------------------------------------------------------------- plan builder"
helper = '''def analyze_cuts(links, env, period, parts, slack_limit=None):
    """Find near-tight separating cuts S (participants P = S & C nonempty, proper).

    Returns list of tuples (S_set, P_set, slack_out, slack_in) with
      slack_out = crossing - sum(r_v, v in P),  slack_in = crossing - sum(r_v, v not in P),
    both >= 0 for feasible instances.  Uses one min-cut per participant for the
    out-form and one for the in-form.
    """
    n = 0
    for (u, v, c) in links:
        n = max(n, u + 1, v + 1)
    for v in parts:
        n = max(n, v + 1)
    D = sum(parts.values())
    sigma, tau = n, n + 1
    total_cap = sum(period * env.get(i, 0) for i in range(len(links)))
    INF = D + total_cap + 1
    participants = sorted(parts)
    C = set(participants)
    found = {}

    def record(S):
        P = S & C
        if not P or P == C:
            return
        crossing = sum(period * env.get(i, 0)
                       for i, (u, v, c) in enumerate(links) if (u in S) != (v in S))
        d1 = sum(parts[v] for v in P)
        d2 = sum(parts[v] for v in C - P)
        so = crossing - d1
        si = crossing - d2
        key = frozenset(S)
        if key not in found or (so + si) < (found[key][2] + found[key][3]):
            found[key] = (S, P, so, si)

    for form in ('out', 'in'):
        for w in participants:
            g = Dinic(n + 2)
            for idx, (a, b, c) in enumerate(links):
                cp = period * env.get(idx, 0)
                if cp > 0:
                    g.add(a, b, cp)
                    g.add(b, a, cp)
            if form == 'out':
                # cut value = crossing + sum(r_v, v not in S)  -> slack_out + D
                for v in participants:
                    if parts[v] > 0:
                        g.add(sigma, v, parts[v])
            else:
                # cut value = crossing + sum(r_v, v in S) -> slack_in + D
                for v in participants:
                    if parts[v] > 0:
                        g.add(v, tau, parts[v])
            g.add(w, tau, INF)
            g.maxflow(sigma, tau)
            S = g.source_side(sigma)
            if w in S:
                continue
            record(S)
    out = []
    for (S, P, so, si) in found.values():
        if slack_limit is not None and min(so, si) > slack_limit:
            continue
        out.append((S, P, so, si))
    out.sort(key=lambda t: (t[2] + t[3]))
    return out


'''
src = src.replace(anchor, helper + anchor)
open('compiler.py','w').write(src)
print('added analyze_cuts')

- **`compiler.py`** — exact-integer witnesses and the plan compiler: capacity witnesses over lease breakpoints; deficient-cut witnesses via min-cut (cross-checked against brute force on random instances); tight-cut analysis feeding sound structural constraints and residual pruning; a backtracking, constraint-aware, randomized tree/route search over weighted logical trees with hash-consed serial-route recipe circuits (concat joins only at forwarders); and a full independent plan verifier.

**Validation**: hand-computed semantic tests, JSON/UTF-8 edge cases, ~2000 randomized traces with independent certificate checking (every `denied`/`blocked` witness and every `prepared` plan re-verified), compiler fuzzing against the exact cut characterization (including adversarially budget-tightened instances through 24–32 participants), and max-schema-size traces (48 vertices, 128 links, 32 participants, 10^12 demands) compiling in ~3 s against the 60 s budget.
